newsitem.title: USA: Key IMM currencies end mixed, June yen up strongly.
newsitem.headline: Key IMM currencies end mixed, June yen up strongly.

text.p: Key IMM currency futures ended a high volume session mixed overall, with June yen's strong performance taking center stage again.

June yen remained at the highest level since late January, in line with overnight strength when the dollar fell to 114.70 yen. Traders said expectations for higher Japanese interest rates and growing concerns that the U.S. Federal Reserve could remain on hold next week kept a lid on lagging dollar/yen.
Traders said a batch of U.S. data Thursday did little to alter the overall sense that players are less certain about what the Fed's policy arm will do when it meets May 20.
Late comments from U.S. Secretary Robert Rubin had minimal impact on the last minutes of futures action, traders said.
Rubin repteated that a strong dollar is in the U.S. interest and said "we have had a strong dollar."
Traders said Chicago Mercantile Exchange price boards showed estimated June yen volume at 37,000 contracts. On Wednesday, June yen traded 28,995, the CME reported.

One trader said a noted fund was an aggressive buyer of June yen futures early, and said interest was brisk all day in yen. Late in the session, he said he saw selling of June Swiss and buying of June marks.
June Canadian dollar futures rallied to a seven-week high, fueled by buy stops and aggressive buying interest from all corners, traders said.
"Basically they're looking for low inflation and strong growth, two pluses that have aided the U.S. dollar," a trader said.

Traders said the Bank of Canada sold Canadian dollars and bought U.S. dollars, but the Canadian dollar rally was undeterred. The intervention came after comments from Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen suggesting that the trend for Canada's currency was positive.

Currency futures shaved overnight gains early Thursday on the U.S. April consumer price index, which rose 0.1 percent overall and 0.3 percent excluding the volatile food and energy sector. Forecasts had been for up 0.1 percent and up 0.2 percent, repsectively.

June yen strengthened slightly later after U.S. April industrial output was reported unchanged and capacity use was reported at 83.4 percent. Forecasts had been for industrial output up 0.2 percent and capacity use at 84.1 percent.

At the close, June yen was up $0.000078 at $0.008665, marks fell $0.0014 to $0.5905, Swiss francs rose $0.0029 to $0.7019, sterling was off $0.0030 at $1.6434, Canadian dollar rose $0.0084 to $0.7301, Australian dollar rose $0.0005 to $0.7776, and Mexican peso was up $0.000225 at $0.125125.
